description: Client + API + server + database, end to end.

screens.body: A full-stack app = client (React) + API (HTTP contract) + server (logic) + database (storage). You now know every piece from this course. This topic connects them into one working system.
screens.heading: The full picture

screens.body: Before code, draw boxes: what screens exist? What endpoints do they need? What tables hold the data? Ten minutes of boxes saves ten hours of rewiring. For SwiftGigs: PostTask screen → POST /api/tasks → tasks table.
screens.heading: Designing the architecture

screens.body: User taps 'Post task' → app sends POST /api/tasks with JSON → server validates, checks auth, inserts into DB → responds 201 with the new task → app adds it to the screen. That round trip is every feature you'll ever build.
screens.heading: The data flow
screens.keyPoint: Every feature is a round trip.

screens.body: Login: client sends email + password via POST. Server checks the hash. Match → server returns a token. The client attaches that token to every future request (Authorization header). Server verifies the token each time. That's auth.

options: A token, sent with every request

screens.heading: Auth flow

screens.body: Test like a user: click through everything. Test like an attacker: empty inputs, giant inputs, wrong types. Test the sad paths — no internet, server error — not just the happy path. Your course grades this; real users live it.
screens.heading: Testing

screens.body: Deploying = putting it where others can reach it. Frontend → Vercel (you did this!). Backend → a host like Render/Fly, or Supabase handles it. Set your env vars on the host BEFORE deploying — remember the build-time lesson.
screens.heading: Deploying

screens.body: Name your pieces: Learn SD's client is React on Vercel. Its 'server' for Byte is Google's Gemini API. SwiftGigs: React client + Supabase backend + database. You can now point at any app and name its four boxes — that's full-stack thinking.
